title: Chuck Mangione labelled jazz; dinners at his family's house
summary: Sam objects to Italian folk songs being labelled jazz and recalls dinners at Mangione's family home in Rochester.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Chuck Macaroni and all this other stuff that we have going on.
Not that I'm taking nothing away from him but I mean that's just the way they've got this stuff projected right now.

So they've got him labeled as one of the great playing jazz bands, great jazz artists and flügelhorns. This man ain't doing nothing b ut playing nothing but Italian folk songs. That's right. And if th'at's got anything to do with jazz, then I'm a monkey's uncle. So they can label it jazz.
That's what they're trying to do now.
That's what they say he is. I know this man ever since he was a small boy man. I was over to his house and his family used to fix those Italian dinners, man.

I saw where an article he had, he wrote in there, he named the artists that used to come to his house to have dinner, Ron Carter, Dizzy Gillespie and a couple of other artists and that was all. Okay, when I was in Dizzy Gillespie's

band, I went to his house to have dinner. When I was in Cannonball's band, I went to his house to have dinner. His father used to send me wine. He used to make the wine down in the cellar. So he used to send me wine. When the people used to be coming from Rochester down this way, you know he'd drop me a jug of wine.

So about four or five years ago, Louis Hayes played in Rochester, as a trio, went out there. I went out to the house to have dinner with the family. But I just say that, it's not that I don't want him to just mention that I've been to his house to have dinner, you know, because I mean I can - if they ever come this way, ever come this way, I invite him and his family at my house for dinner and I give them what I have. It's just the fact where the man just don't tell it like it is, man. I don't give a damn, you know what I mean.
In fact he don't even talk about his brother, man.
That's right. He has a very strange attitude. I've heard all kinds of reports about him.

Shit, man but I mean like I said, that's the same thing. Just don't take our music and say you're playing the jazz music man because you aren't playing the jazz music. You are not playing the jazz music. You're not playing the kind of blues we play. See black people music....
